english: Sweet mead, sweetness of the gods. In the cauldron, of honey, you are born. Gods and men drink you, dear one. You are the great joy of the immortals. Now we pour out the first share to the gods. Now we drink you from full cups.
uncertain: ǵn̥h₁yéth₂e read as 2sg middle 'you are born'
m̥lités read as gen. sg. 'of honey'

english: The tongues (or tongue) of the fire are red. It licks the fat and devours the meat. From it black smoke rises up. The gods smell the smoke and come. May the Fire burn for the immortals.
uncertain: dn̥ǵʰwéh₂s with fem. sg. adjective h₁rudʰréh₂: number unclear
sélpos léyǵʰti: subject or object unclear

english: Milk the cow in the morning. Heat the milk at the fire. Pour the hot milk into the fire. Give the dog the leftover.
Whoever pours, he gives the first cup to the gods. Then the old man drinks, then the young men sip. Whoever does not follow, may Perkwunos not hear him.
uncertain: srobʰéyōnti has an -éye- (causative-looking) stem for plain 'sip'

english: Lead the fattened ram. Cut it with the knife. Pour its blood onto the earth. Cook the meat on the coals. Give the first share to the god and burn the fat in the fire. Then the free men eat the meat.
uncertain: gʷoh₂móm and gʷrúsu unfamiliar; guessed 'fattened' and 'coals'

english: Put honey and water into the cauldron. Heat the cauldron at the fire. It will ferment for three days. Then pour the mead. Do not drink the first cup; give it to the god.
